section_summary: This section of the file primarily documents inquiries and detailed consular reporting regarding the rapid emergence and expansion of Japan's staple fiber (artificial wool) and rayon industries between 1934 and 1936. Spurred by queries from New York textile consultant Joseph D. Holmes, the American Consulate General at Tokyo produced two comprehensive investigative reports (Nos. 140 and 167) analyzing Japanese staple fiber manufacturing facilities, production capacities, government subsidies, and commercial applications. The file also covers trade interest and media attention following the leak of the December 1935 consular report to the Daily News Record, as well as an unrelated initial inquiry concerning the sale of Japanese patent and trademark rights for the Sanforizing process.

subfiles.about: George R. Coleman discusses his planned trip to Japan to sell Sanforizing patent and trademark rights to a Japanese firm such as Mitsui.
subfiles.summary: George R. Coleman of Elbrook Inc. informed State Department officers of his intention to sell Cluett, Peabody & Co.'s Sanforizing patent and trademark rights in Japan rather than license them. Eugene H. Dooman questioned the wisdom of an outright sale.
subfiles.title: Memorandum of Conversation: Selling to a Japanese Concern Patent and Trade-mark Rights to a Sanforizing Process for Cotton and Silk Textiles

subfiles.about: Transmittal of a memorandum of conversation with George R. Coleman concerning the sale of Sanforizing patent and trademark rights in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Transmits for the Ambassador's information a memorandum of conversation with George R. Coleman regarding Sanforizing patent rights.
subfiles.title: Instruction No. 987 to the American Ambassador at Tokyo

subfiles.about: Cross-reference note regarding Japanese timber purchases in Vancouver to supply raw materials for rayon pulp.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference note concerning timber purchases in Vancouver by Nisso Rayon Pulp Company to prevent raw material shortages.
subfiles.title: Document File Note: Purchase of Timber by Nisso Rayon Pulp Co.

subfiles.about: Inquiry from mill consultant Joseph D. Holmes regarding reports of artificial wool manufacturing developments in Japan.

subfiles.about: Informs Joseph D. Holmes that consular officers in Japan have been instructed to investigate artificial wool developments.
subfiles.summary: Acknowledges Holmes's letter, states consular officers in Japan have been instructed to investigate, and cites earlier consular reports from Nagoya on the woolen and rayon industries available through the Department of Commerce.
subfiles.title: Letter to Joseph D. Holmes regarding Japanese Artificial Wool Inquiries

subfiles.about: Directs the Consul General at Tokyo to prepare and submit a report on Japanese artificial wool developments.
subfiles.summary: Transmits Joseph D. Holmes's inquiry and instructs the Consul General to prepare a report promptly.
subfiles.title: Instruction to the American Consul General at Tokyo regarding Artificial Wool

subfiles.about: Directs the Consul at Kobe to prepare and submit a report on Japanese artificial wool developments.
subfiles.summary: Transmits Joseph D. Holmes's letter and instructs the Consul at Kobe to report on artificial wool.
subfiles.title: Instruction to the American Consul at Kobe regarding Artificial Wool

subfiles.about: Directs the Consul at Nagoya to prepare and submit a report on Japanese artificial wool developments.
subfiles.summary: Transmits Joseph D. Holmes's letter and instructs the Consul at Nagoya to report on artificial wool.
subfiles.title: Instruction to the American Consul at Nagoya regarding Artificial Wool

subfiles.about: Internal memorandum noting that Kobe's despatch regarding artificial wool requires no action because Tokyo is preparing the report.
subfiles.summary: Notes that the Kobe despatch requires no action since the inquiry was transferred to Tokyo.
subfiles.title: Department of State Internal Note on Kobe Despatch

subfiles.about: Consul Howard Donovan reports that information on artificial wool is difficult to obtain and notes Tokyo is preparing a comprehensive report.
subfiles.summary: Explains local difficulties in obtaining data on artificial wool and states that Holmes's inquiry was referred to the Consulate General at Tokyo, which is preparing a comprehensive report.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 287 from Kobe: Production of Artificial Wool in Japan

subfiles.about: Comprehensive consular survey detailing the experimental progress, production capacity, and manufacturing firms of staple fiber in Japan.
subfiles.summary: This consular report examines the rapid growth of Japan's staple fiber (artificial wool) industry, initiated to compensate for domestic deficiencies in wool and cotton. Daily national production is estimated at four to five metric tons, with forecasts projecting fifty tons daily by mid-1935. It details activities across major industrial centers and profiles operating and planned manufacturing companies, including Kurashiki, Kinka, Nisshin, Shinko, Nitto, Dai-Nippon, and Nippon Keori.
subfiles.title: Report No. 140: Production of Staple Fiber (Artificial Wool) in Japan

subfiles.about: Transmittal of a copy of the Tokyo Consulate General's May 28, 1934 report on staple fiber in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Transmits a copy of the Tokyo Consulate General's report of May 28, 1934 on staple fiber.
subfiles.title: Letter to Joseph D. Holmes Transmitting Tokyo Report on Staple Fiber

subfiles.about: Requests that the Tokyo Consulate General provide additional samples of staple fiber.
subfiles.summary: Requests a few additional samples of the artificial wool enclosed with the May 28, 1934 report.
subfiles.title: Instruction to the American Consul General at Tokyo Requesting Additional Fiber Samples

subfiles.about: Joseph D. Holmes expresses appreciation for the Tokyo report and asks to receive samples of synthetic wool and yarn for analysis.
subfiles.summary: Praises the Tokyo report and requests portions of the synthetic wool and yarn samples for technical textile analysis.
subfiles.title: Letter from Joseph D. Holmes Requesting Staple Fiber Samples

subfiles.about: Follow-up letter from Joseph D. Holmes requesting samples of staple fiber and yarn mentioned in the Tokyo report.
subfiles.summary: Reiterates request for samples of staple fiber and yarn mentioned in Tokyo report No. 140.
subfiles.title: Letter from Joseph D. Holmes Reiterating Request for Staple Fiber Samples

subfiles.about: Informs Joseph D. Holmes that original samples were sent to government agencies and additional samples have been requested from Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: Explains that original samples went to government agencies and promises additional samples requested from Tokyo upon arrival.
subfiles.title: Letter to Joseph D. Holmes regarding Availability of Fiber Samples

subfiles.about: Joseph D. Holmes stresses the eagerness of textile experts to examine even small samples of Japanese staple fiber.
subfiles.summary: Emphasizes that textile industry experts are anxious to examine even small samples of Japanese synthetic fiber and yarn.
subfiles.title: Letter from Joseph D. Holmes Emphasizing Urgency of Obtaining Samples

subfiles.about: Joseph D. Holmes asks which government organizations received the Japanese staple fiber samples.
subfiles.summary: Asks which government organizations received the Tokyo staple fiber samples so he may contact them directly.

subfiles.about: Informs Joseph D. Holmes that the Tokyo report was sent to Agriculture and Commerce, and the samples went to Commerce.

subfiles.summary: Transmits additional samples of Japanese staple fiber in response to the Department's instruction of July 5, 1934.
subfiles.title: Despatch from Tokyo: Transmitting Additional Samples of Staple Fiber

subfiles.about: Transmittal of the requested Japanese artificial wool samples to Joseph D. Holmes.
subfiles.summary: Transmits to Holmes the requested samples of Japanese artificial wool obtained from the Tokyo Consulate General.
subfiles.title: Letter to Joseph D. Holmes Transmitting Staple Fiber Samples

subfiles.about: Joseph D. Holmes encloses a trade clipping and asks the Department to investigate whether artificial wool is being used commercially in fabrics.
subfiles.summary: Encloses a news clipping and asks whether Japanese mills are using artificial wool in fabrics as a wool substitute.
subfiles.title: Letter from Joseph D. Holmes Requesting Investigation into Uses of Artificial Wool

subfiles.about: Instructs the Consul General at Tokyo to investigate how artificial wool is being used in manufactured textiles in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Instructs the Consul General to investigate and report how artificial wool is being used in Japanese fabrics.
subfiles.title: Instruction to the American Consul General at Tokyo regarding Uses of Artificial Wool

subfiles.about: Informs Joseph D. Holmes that the Tokyo Consulate General has been instructed to investigate the commercial uses of artificial wool.
subfiles.summary: Informs Holmes that his inquiry has been referred to the Tokyo Consulate General for investigation and report.
subfiles.title: Letter to Joseph D. Holmes regarding Inquiry on Uses of Artificial Wool

subfiles.about: Comprehensive consular report analyzing production capacity, commercial applications, military uses, subsidies, and export markets for Japanese staple fiber.
subfiles.summary: Prepared by Consul Charles A. Hutchinson, this report updates the May 1934 survey and provides an extensive analysis of Japan's staple fiber industry. Seven commercial producers maintain a daily capacity of 36.5 metric tons, supplemented by twelve experimental and five projected companies. Staple fiber is increasingly blended with cotton, wool, silk, and linen for kimono and suit fabrics, while the Japanese government provides subsidies and military agencies test it for uniforms and explosives. Monthly exports have reached 300,000 pounds, primarily destined for Germany and the United States, raising concerns over potential market overproduction.
subfiles.title: Report No. 167: Report on Production and Use of Staple Fibre in Japan

subfiles.about: Transmittal of the Tokyo report of December 11, 1935, and woven fabric samples to Joseph D. Holmes.
subfiles.summary: Encloses Tokyo report No. 167 and sends woven cloth samples for temporary inspection before government distribution.
subfiles.title: Letter to Joseph D. Holmes Transmitting Tokyo Report and Woven Fabric Samples

subfiles.about: Discusses articles in the Daily News Record quoting the confidential Tokyo staple fiber report and highlighting Japanese subsidies and import competition.
subfiles.summary: Roy Veatch alerts Herbert Feis that the Daily News Record published detailed quotations from the December 11, 1935 Tokyo consular report. The articles emphasized Japanese government subsidies and surging imports, prompting a recommended checkup by Far Eastern Affairs to identify the source of the leak.
subfiles.title: Memorandum regarding Press Leak of Tokyo Staple Fiber Report

subfiles.about: Internal departmental routing slip from the Division of Research and Publication.
subfiles.summary: Department routing slip from the Division of Research and Publication transferring correspondence.
subfiles.title: Routing Slip: Division of Research and Publication

subfiles.about: H. S. Davis requests a copy of the State Department's special report on Japanese staple fiber mentioned in the Daily News Record.
subfiles.summary: Requests a copy of the State Department's report on the Japanese staple fiber industry cited in the press.
subfiles.title: Letter from H. S. Davis Requesting Report on Japanese Rayon Staple Fiber Industry
subfiles.to: Division of Public Information, Department of State

subfiles.about: Informs H. S. Davis that no copies of the Tokyo report are available for distribution, noting the Daily News Record published most of it.
subfiles.summary: Informs Davis that report copies are unavailable for public distribution, though the Daily News Record published most contents.
subfiles.title: Letter to H. S. Davis regarding Unavailability of Tokyo Report

subfiles.about: Press report publishing extensive extracts from the Tokyo consular report on Japan's staple fiber production, government subsidies, and price competition.
subfiles.summary: Published in the Daily News Record, this article details findings from the Tokyo consular report of December 11, 1935. It highlights Japanese government subsidies, expanding daily production capacity, low export prices, and the competitive threat Japanese staple fiber poses to domestic cotton and wool markets.
subfiles.title: Clipping from Daily News Record: U. S. State Department Reports Japan Government Staple Subsidy

subfiles.summary: Requests a copy of the Tokyo consular report of December 11, 1935 on Japanese staple fiber.
subfiles.title: Letter from William Ries Requesting Tokyo Report on Staple Fiber

subfiles.about: Informs William Ries that his request for the Tokyo report has been referred to the Department of Commerce.
